questions.question: Why does AI procurement need more than feature comparison?
options: Because the vendor demo already covers every enterprise control a buyer needs to verify
Because contract terms are standardised across AI vendors, so only features distinguish them
Because data handling, security, integration, lock-in, and operating cost affect long-term risk
Because security evidence is supplied later by the vendor's compliance team on request
questions.explanation: AI vendor decisions create operating, security, and commercial consequences. The comparison has to cover enterprise controls, integration, operating model, support, and cost behavior.

questions.question: A vendor demo went well and the team wants to move. What has the evaluation not yet covered?
options: Model accuracy, response latency, prompt formatting, and supported output schema options
User interface design, onboarding effort, in-app help quality, and mobile app availability on every platform
Data residency, integration ownership, audit evidence, pricing behavior, and exit strategy
Training-data provenance, model size, fine-tuning support, and open-weight release policy
questions.explanation: The lesson names exactly these gaps behind a strong demo: data residency, integration ownership, audit evidence, pricing behavior, and exit strategy. The decision feels fast but creates long-term risk.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
options: A ranked vendor-fit plan with matched controls and rationale per option
A signed contract once the highest-scoring vendor clears the scorecard
A procurement system that routes approvals through the finance department
A guaranteed approval that the shortlisted vendor meets security policy
questions.explanation: The artifact supports evaluation by ranking vendor fit and matching controls. It does not replace procurement, security review, or the contract itself.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
options: A trial that runs without pre-agreed criteria, so the team stays open to what it finds
A pricing assumption carried straight from the demo, since the list price rarely changes between renewals
A vendor scorecard that compares security, data handling, integration, cost, and lock-in
A decision record that names the winner but leaves the exit path to a later discussion
questions.explanation: A vendor scorecard makes comparison explicit across security, data handling, integration, cost, and lock-in. Trial criteria, an exit plan, and an approval record are the other controls this lesson teaches.

questions.question: When should a vendor decision require stronger controls?
options: When security, data handling, lock-in, or pricing uncertainty is high
Only when the vendor is a startup rather than an established supplier with a long track record
Only when the integration touches more than one system at go-live
Only when the contract value crosses the department's approval limit
questions.explanation: High uncertainty and risk require stronger trial and approval controls. Vendor size and contract value are not the signals this lesson scores.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an exit plan?
options: To document how the trial will be scored once the proof of concept ends
To record which internal team owns the integration after the rollout
To capture the pricing scenarios the finance team asked to be compared
To make lock-in risk visible and reducible before committing to a vendor
questions.explanation: Exit planning makes lock-in visible before purchase. The lesson asks that every vendor decision carry one.
